description:
## Why

Add the framework-not-policy stance to AGENTS.md `## Non-negotiable constraints` so future agents and contributors don't drift back into encoding CA/B Forum / DoD / vendor-root-program policies in the main crates.

## What

Append a new non-negotiable constraint (number 5):

> 5. **Framework, not policy.** The workspace ships standards-based mechanisms (Profile trait, Lint trait, ValidationPolicy, DeviationStore, etc.) and RFC / ITU-T / NIST baseline implementations. It does NOT ship canonical encodings of any single organization's policy — CA/B Forum, DoD, Mozilla / Apple / Microsoft root programs, or individual CA CPSs. CA/B Forum reference implementations live in sibling `-cabf` crates (`pkix-profiles-cabf`, `pkix-lint-cabf`) marked 'reference / not authoritative.' Adding new vendor or industry-forum policy encodings to the main crates requires explicit human approval.

Also update the `## What this is` section to list the new `-cabf` reference crates once they exist (this child should land **after** PKIX-amgn.2 and PKIX-amgn.3 add the crates, OR as a single coordinated commit).

## Acceptance

- [ ] New non-negotiable constraint #5 in AGENTS.md.
- [ ] `## What this is` mentions the `-cabf` reference crates once they exist (coordination with .2 and .3).
- [ ] Existing constraints 1-4 unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Encoding the line precisely for every edge case (e.g. is RFC 6125 'TLS identity verification' a policy decision? we've decided yes for the universal serverAuth EKU bit, no for hostname matching — but this is in the epic body, not the AGENTS.md text).

## Filed as

Anchor child of PKIX-amgn.
title: AGENTS.md: encode framework-not-policy stance as non-negotiable
